idiom_name: no weak/strong distinction - non-owning pointer plus an explicit invalidation contract (GWeakRef / g_object_weak_ref under GLib)
implementation_notes: C has no garbage collector, so nothing keeps a referent alive in the first place and the pattern's central distinction - an edge that does not extend a lifetime, promoted atomically to a strong reference - has no language-level carrier: a plain pointer is already non-owning, but it becomes dangling the moment the owner frees, and no check can tell a live pointer from a freed one. What replaces the classic structure is an explicit ownership contract: the owner publishes a destroy or detach notification and every holder registers (or removes itself) before freeing - exactly what GLib models for GObject, where g_object_weak_ref adds a callback invoked before the object is freed and GWeakRef is a thread-safe weak reference whose g_weak_ref_get atomically acquires a strong reference or returns NULL. Use those when GLib is already in the stack; otherwise hand-write the same protocol around a mutex-protected registry and document that the pointer is valid only inside the ownership protocol.
pitfalls: A bare pointer is not a weak reference: after free() it dangles and there is no way to test liveness - the owner must notify (g_object_weak_ref) or the holder must be able to promote atomically under a lock (GWeakRef).
g_object_weak_ref callbacks are documented as not thread-safe and run before the object's dispose; if the last g_object_unref can happen on another thread, use GWeakRef instead.
A hand-rolled registry must be protected by the same lock as the destruction path, otherwise a holder can promote a pointer that is being freed concurrently.
alternative: There is no collector to weaken, so give the owner an explicit destroy-notification contract: holders register and are invalidated before the target is freed, and a non-owning pointer is valid only inside that protocol. Use GWeakRef / g_object_weak_ref when GLib is present, or share lifetimes through reference counting (g_object_ref/unref, intrusive refcounts) and keep borrowed pointers documented as borrowed.
